doc.title: Marty Sheller interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 9, 2022

title: Producers and Mongo's Columbia albums
summary: Good relations with producers; Mitch Miller assigned Robert Mercy to Mongo, yielding 'In the Mood' cha-cha, and a later under-marketed album.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: How has your relationship been with producers over the years?

Pretty good because generally they respect my abilities and they respect my comments and suggestions. So I haven’t had any problems. Like maybe I just haven’t run into the wrong kind of people, but it’s pretty good.
I think I read something about when Mongo’s band got signed to Columbia, that Mitch Miller assigned a producer that didn’t quite get it.

Yes. He assigned a fellow by the way who is a terrific musician named Robert Mercy who wrote for Andy Williams and other artists, I mean a really good musician. But to give him the job of producing a Mongo album, we all were like what? You know and sure enough he chose material that was not typically Mongo material and tried to make it into something commercial and it just, as far as we were concerned, it just didn’t work. I’m trying to think of the name of the song, I can’t think of it, but [scats]
That kind of says it all.

You know I sometimes use that, that’s very curious you say that because when I’m trying to show students what I means to swing eighth notes I’ll use “In the Mood.” And you know, play it like we know it and then I’ll go now what if we straighten out the eighth notes [scats].

I did one arrangement on that album. I did an arrangement of “Walk on By” on that album but Bob, Robert Mercy did all the rest. And as a matter of fact, Mongo, when he signed with them he said he wanted to do a typical Latin album using different rhythms. And they said, “Well no, let Bob Mercy, we want him to do an album, and then we promise that after that then you can do what you want to do.” And the second one was an album that Mongo did, I’m trying to think the name of it, I can see the cover, a green cover with a girl’s face on it which was one of the most under-the-radar records, it’s a terrific record. Really terrific. But they didn’t know how to market at that point, they didn’t know how to market that kind of an album so nothing ever happened. It’s a shame because it was a really, really terrific album.
